questions.q: Who was the long-reigning Sultan of Oman who died in 2020?
questions.why: He ruled for almost 50 years.

questions.q: Who became Sultan of Oman in 2020?
questions.why: He is Qaboos's cousin.

questions.q: Which East African island did Oman once rule as part of its empire?
questions.why: Sultan Said moved his court there in the 1830s.

questions.q: What did ancient Oman export that was worth more than gold?
questions.why: It grows in the Dhofar region.

questions.q: Which country's influence ended in Muscat when Omanis expelled it in 1650?
questions.why: The Portuguese had held Muscat since 1507.

questions.q: In which year did Sultan Qaboos come to power?
questions.why: He began a period called the Renaissance.

questions.q: Which 1960s–70s rebellion took place in the Dhofar region?
questions.why: It ended in 1976.

questions.q: Which dynasty has ruled Oman since 1744?
questions.why: Ahmad bin Said founded it.

questions.q: Which ancient irrigation channels are a UNESCO site?
questions.why: Some are over 1,000 years old.

questions.q: Which ancient city at Sumhuram traded frankincense?
questions.why: It is part of the Land of Frankincense UNESCO site.

questions.q: Which legendary sailor is said to have come from the Omani port of Sohar?
questions.why: Sohar was a great medieval port.

questions.q: Which forts guard Muscat's old harbour?
questions.why: The Portuguese built them in the 1580s.

questions.q: Which UNESCO-listed oasis fort is one of Oman's oldest?
questions.why: It dates back to the 1200s.

questions.q: Which 'lost city' in the desert is linked to Ubar of legend?
questions.why: It was found with help from satellite images.

questions.q: Which Bronze Age tombs at Bat are a UNESCO site?
questions.why: They date to the third millennium BC.

questions.q: What is the capital of Oman?
questions.why: It sits between mountains and the sea.

questions.q: Which strait does Oman's Musandam peninsula overlook?
questions.why: It is called the 'Norway of Arabia' for its fjords.

questions.q: Which southern city is famous for its monsoon season, the khareef?
questions.why: The hills turn green each summer.

questions.q: Which sea lies off Oman's eastern coast?
questions.why: Turtles nest on its beaches.

questions.q: Which mountain range includes Jebel Shams?
questions.why: Jebel Shams is Oman's highest peak.

questions.q: Which canyon near Jebel Shams is called the 'Grand Canyon of Arabia'?
questions.why: It is about 1,000 m deep.

questions.q: Which town on the coast is famous for building dhows?
questions.why: Turtles nest nearby at Ras al-Jinz.

questions.q: Which old capital is famous for its fort and Friday goat market?
questions.why: It was Oman's capital in the 600s and 700s.

questions.q: Which desert of rolling dunes lies east of Ibra?
questions.why: Bedouin camps welcome visitors.

questions.q: Which beach reserve is famous for green turtles?
questions.why: Thousands nest there each year.

questions.q: Which Omani opera house opened in Muscat in 2011?
questions.why: It was the first in the Gulf.

questions.q: What is Oman's currency?
questions.why: It is one of the most valuable currencies.

questions.q: Which huge mosque in Muscat has one of the world's largest carpets?
questions.why: It opened in 2001.

questions.q: Which curved dagger is Oman's national symbol?
questions.why: It appears on the flag.

questions.q: Which slow-cooked meat dish is made for Eid in an underground oven?
questions.why: It cooks for up to two days.
